question: Can diffusion guidance trade off sample fidelity and diversity without a separately trained classifier?
hypothesis: Mixing conditional and jointly trained unconditional score estimates gives an FID/IS tradeoff similar to classifier guidance.
contributions: Classifier-free guidance: jointly train a conditional and an unconditional diffusion model in one network and combine their scores at sampling time.
Empirical FID/IS tradeoff on 64x64 and 128x128 ImageNet, with ablations over p_uncond and sampling steps T.

method.summary: A single class-conditional diffusion network is trained with the class label replaced by a null token with probability p_uncond. At sampling the guided score (1+w)*eps(z,c) - w*eps(z) is used. Evaluated on area-downsampled class-conditional ImageNet at 64x64 and 128x128.

models.name: Classifier-free guided diffusion model (64x64)
models.architecture: same architecture and hyperparameters as ADM-G (Dhariwal & Nichol 2021), continuous time training, eps-prediction

training.objective: E[||eps_theta(z_lambda, c) - eps||^2] with c replaced by null token with probability p_uncond; lambda ~ p(lambda) hyperbolic-secant-like, lambda = -2 log tan(a u + b)

other.hyperparameters: same as Dhariwal & Nichol (2021) guided diffusion, not listed

inference.decoding: ancestral sampler with log-SNR-interpolated variance, v constant; DDIM mentioned as replaceable
inference.samples: 50000 samples per guidance value for FID/IS

parameters.T: 128/256/1024 on 128x128 (Fig 5 legend says 512 instead of 1024); 64x64 T not stated
parameters.guided_score: (1+w)*eps(z,c) - w*eps(z); two forward passes per step

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance following Heusel et al. 2017, 50000 samples

metrics.name: IS
metrics.definition: Inception Score following Salimans et al. 2016, 50000 samples

eval.protocol: Sweep w; one model per setting; no seeds or confidence intervals reported.

evidence.quote: The 64 × 64 models used sampler noise interpolation coefficient v = 0.3 and were trained for 400 thousand steps; the 128 × 128 models used v = 0.2 and were trained for 2.7 million steps.

results.claim: Best FID on 64x64 comes at almost no guidance (p_uncond=0.1, w=0.1).
results.table: Table 1, row w = 0.1, column FID, p_uncond=0.1

results.claim: At w=4.0 on 64x64 FID degrades to 26.22 while IS reaches 260.2.
results.table: Table 1, row w = 4.0, columns FID/IS, p_uncond=0.1 (26.22, 260.2)

results.claim: p_uncond=0.5 is consistently worse than 0.1 and 0.2, which are about equal.
results.table: Table 1, row w = 0.0, column FID, p_uncond=0.5 (2.21)

results.claim: On 128x128 FID 2.43 at w=0.3, beating ADM-G (2.97).
results.table: Table 2, row w = 0.3, column FID, T=256 (2.43)

results.claim: At w=4.0 on 128x128 the model beats BigGAN-deep at max-IS truncation on both FID and IS.
results.table: Table 2, row w = 4.0, columns FID/IS, T=256 (21.53, 421.03)

results.claim: T=256 gives a good quality/speed balance; each step needs two model evaluations, so the compute-fair setting is T=128, which underperforms ADM-G on FID.
results.table: Table 2, row w = 0.3, column FID, T=128 (3.04)
results.note: At T=128, w=0.4 gives 3.02, also above 2.97.

limits: Proof of concept only; hyperparameters were tuned for classifier guidance and may be suboptimal.
Two forward passes per sampling step make it slower than classifier guidance.
Reduced diversity may be unacceptable where underrepresented data matter.
Only class-conditional ImageNet; no text conditioning tested.
No optimizer, learning rate, batch size, parameter count or hardware stated; no seeds or error bars.
